exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. PyTorch stable documentation reviewed 2026-09-19 (current docs identified as 2.14).

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; typed recall and coding questions provide the scored retrieval signal.

authoring_notes: This is a practical learning track, not a certification. Domain weights are curriculum emphasis weights used for adaptive selection. Learning placeholders are exact cloze versions of their revealed text. Reviewed against PyTorch 2.14-era official documentation and the app's structured typed-fill code/table renderer on 2026-09-19.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Current PyTorch provides `__________` APIs to query an available accelerator such as CUDA, MPS, XPU, or other supported backends.

reveal.text: Current PyTorch provides `torch.accelerator` APIs to query an available accelerator such as CUDA, MPS, XPU, or other supported backends.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A current quickstart pattern uses the available accelerator when present and otherwise __________.

reveal.text: A current quickstart pattern uses the available accelerator when present and otherwise falls back to CPU.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Selecting a device is only part of the job; model parameters and input tensors must __________ to that device.

reveal.text: Selecting a device is only part of the job; model parameters and input tensors must also be moved to that device.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` moves registered model parameters and buffers, while input tensors usually need their own `.to(device)` call.

reveal.text: `model.to(device)` moves registered model parameters and buffers, while input tensors usually need their own `.to(device)` call.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Move __________ to compatible devices before running operations between them.

reveal.text: Move both model and batch tensors to compatible devices before running operations between them.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Moving only the model or only the data commonly causes __________ errors.

reveal.text: Moving only the model or only the data commonly causes device-mismatch errors.

source_refs.title: Move model and data together — PyTorch documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A recommended PyTorch pattern saves `__________` rather than serializing the entire Python model object.

reveal.text: A recommended PyTorch pattern saves `model.state_dict()` rather than serializing the entire Python model object.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use `__________(model.state_dict(), path)` to persist model weights and buffers.

reveal.text: Use `torch.save(model.state_dict(), path)` to persist model weights and buffers.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Saving only the state dict means the model __________ in code before loading those weights.

reveal.text: Saving only the state dict means the model architecture must be recreated in code before loading those weights.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: To restore a state dict, recreate the model architecture and call `model.__________(...)` with the loaded mapping.

reveal.text: To restore a state dict, recreate the model architecture and call `model.load_state_dict(...)` with the loaded mapping.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: When loading a weights file, `torch.load(..., __________)` limits loading to weights-oriented objects and is a recommended safety practice.

reveal.text: When loading a weights file, `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` limits loading to weights-oriented objects and is a recommended safety practice.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Loading a state dict __________ `model.eval()`; choose train or eval mode explicitly for the next use.

reveal.text: Loading a state dict does not automatically call `model.eval()`; choose train or eval mode explicitly for the next use.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A resumable training checkpoint commonly stores the model state dict, __________, current epoch or step, and other training state you need to continue.

reveal.text: A resumable training checkpoint commonly stores the model state dict, optimizer state dict, current epoch or step, and other training state you need to continue.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Optimizer state matters because adaptive optimizers and momentum methods keep __________ beyond model weights.

reveal.text: Optimizer state matters because adaptive optimizers and momentum methods keep internal state beyond model weights.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Saving only model weights is enough for inference but may __________ a seamless training resume.

reveal.text: Saving only model weights is enough for inference but may not reproduce a seamless training resume.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` runs eligible operations in selected lower precision while keeping other operations in higher precision as appropriate.

reveal.text: `torch.autocast` runs eligible operations in selected lower precision while keeping other operations in higher precision as appropriate.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Wrap the __________ computation in an autocast context when using automatic mixed precision.

reveal.text: Wrap the forward pass and loss computation in an autocast context when using automatic mixed precision.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ itself inside autocast; backward uses the dtypes chosen for the corresponding forward operations.

reveal.text: Do not place backward itself inside autocast; backward uses the dtypes chosen for the corresponding forward operations.

source_refs.title: Automatic mixed precision autocast — PyTorch documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `torch.amp.__________` scales the loss and gradients to reduce float16 gradient underflow during mixed-precision training.

reveal.text: `torch.amp.GradScaler` scales the loss and gradients to reduce float16 gradient underflow during mixed-precision training.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A common CUDA sequence is `scaler.scale(loss).backward()`, `scaler.step(optimizer)`, then `__________`.

reveal.text: A common CUDA sequence is `scaler.scale(loss).backward()`, `scaler.step(optimizer)`, then `scaler.update()`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: GradScaler is not required for ordinary full-precision training and is __________ autocast.

reveal.text: GradScaler is not required for ordinary full-precision training and is not needed for inference-only autocast.

source_refs.title: Gradient scaling for float16 AMP — PyTorch documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` returns an optimized callable around a model or Python function using PyTorch compilation infrastructure.

reveal.text: `torch.compile` returns an optimized callable around a model or Python function using PyTorch compilation infrastructure.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A simple entry point is `compiled_model = __________` and then calling the compiled model normally.

reveal.text: A simple entry point is `compiled_model = torch.compile(model)` and then calling the compiled model normally.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Compilation can add startup overhead and graph breaks, so __________ end-to-end performance instead of assuming every workload becomes faster.

reveal.text: Compilation can add startup overhead and graph breaks, so measure end-to-end performance instead of assuming every workload becomes faster.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Reproducible PyTorch experiments often begin by __________ random generators, while stricter determinism may require additional backend or algorithm settings.

reveal.text: Reproducible PyTorch experiments often begin by seeding random generators, while stricter determinism may require additional backend or algorithm settings.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________, software versions, data splits, and hyperparameters when you need to compare experiments reliably.

reveal.text: Record seeds, software versions, data splits, and hyperparameters when you need to compare experiments reliably.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Exact reproducibility is __________ across PyTorch releases, platforms, or all CPU and accelerator operations.

reveal.text: Exact reproducibility is not guaranteed across PyTorch releases, platforms, or all CPU and accelerator operations.
